correctness.rationale: Complete 32768-frequency integer Walsh transform of 2000 directly enumerated spanning trees agrees, at every frequency, with a separate exact Bareiss evaluation of the signed weighted reduced Laplacian. The 396 S5 signing-orbit certificate partitions all signings. Weighted matrix-tree and Walsh diagonalization prove the multiplier interpretation; Parseval, histogram, gcd, and second Fourier support-transform sums are independently checked. Translation averaging proves minimality over arbitrary real or complex endpoint projections. No extrapolation beyond the fixed graph.

originality.rationale: The comparison separates signed spanning-tree Fourier coefficients from switching-invariant signed-graph polynomials and from other graphs' Fourier tree spectra. Closest accessible primary full texts are Zaslavsky (2012, open 2013) and Beck et al. (2013), whose stated theorems concern switching classes and chromatic polynomials. A weighted tree source from 2003 supplies general determinant machinery only in the material inspected. The previously published Petersen pivot-exchange study enumerates the same 2000 trees but has a different operator. Neither the signed tree multiplier histogram nor the unrestricted range-projection norm is implied by the sources examined. Unindexed or abstract-only sources remain a priority risk.
residual_risks: Older signed weighted Petersen spanning-tree enumeration tables outside retrieved sources could contain some values.
The Martin–Reiner full text and the Petersen pivot-exchange article full text were not inspected, so no whole-document noncoverage inference is made for those items.
The exact evaluated finite result may have been independently recorded in unpublished software or unindexed tables.

value.rationale: The Petersen graph is a canonical highly symmetric nonplanar cubic graph. Its complete signed-tree Fourier support governs inversion and stable projection in the Boolean edge cube, not merely ordinary tree enumeration or switching-invariant signed-graph theory. Exact rank 18856 of 32768, minimum positive Fourier gap 16, and the sharp unrestricted endpoint range-projection norm 36651/1024 are natural unknown stability invariants; the complete finite classification has independent determinant and orbit certificates. No claim of a general graph-family breakthrough is required or made.
